them back after a restart.
# dsh-pause-resume
One button in the DeepSeek Harness session header. It stops what is running — asking a running turn

to wrap up first — writes a small plan to disk, and after a restart the same button puts that work
b

rap up first — writes a small plan to disk, and after a restart the same button puts that work
back.

* ⏸ — work is running. Press to stop it.
* ▶ — work is stopped, or a previous process left work to r

estore. Press to restore it.
* ↻ — a turn stopped on its own. Press to continue what did not finish.
* ⏸ dimmed — nothing to stop, restore or continue.
The glyph is the only status. There is no counter, no panel, no badge and no toast, because a second
indicator would be a second source of truth for the same fact. When the last press left something f

or
a person to look at, the one-sentence tooltip says so and the button still offers the same glyph.
## What it restores
| Work | Pause | Restore |
| A session with an unfinished turn | turn wrapped up or cancelled, session recorded | session mount

ed, then one visible continuation message |
| A goal that was armed | paused with the revision it ha

d | `goals.resume` with that exact revision; the goal driver continues on its own |
| A session that

only carried that goal | recorded, nothing stopped | mounted; the resumed goal takes over |
| A run
ning background job | killed and recorded | recorded only: a job is a live process, not replayable,

so the continuation message names it and the turn restarts it if the work still needs it |
| A sessi

on that ended normally | untouched | untouched, and never recorded in the first place |
| A terminal

/ finished session | untouched | untouched |
| A schedule | untouched | untouched |
Schedules are not paused: the schedule service has no disable operation, only delete, and deleting a
person's schedule to pause it is not a trade this plugin makes. A schedule that fires while paused
starts a turn, but the button keeps showing ▶ while a pause plan waits: a pending plan owns the main
action, so the only honest next step is to finish the restore. The schedule appears in that restore
summary like any other work started after the press.
## What a pause does
A press does not cancel at once. It first asks the turn that is running to wrap up, and cancels only
what is still running when the window closes: `wrapUpMs` (default 3000; `0` cancels immediately, as
every version before 0.9.0 did). A turn that ends inside the window is stopped as completed; the re

st
are cancelled when the time is up, so a pause still never leaves a turn running behind it. Either

way
the plan is written and the sessions are recorded, and the next step is the same: press ▶ to re

store,
or restart and let the plan be picked up. When something had to be cancelled, the tooltip say

s the
work to continue is saved; when everything wrapped up by itself, it says nothing extra.
If the window closes with the steer still unread, the press takes it back: a pause that did not happ

en
must not replay later as a fresh instruction in the restored session. Only that one message is
re

moved, only for sessions that timed out, and only while it is still queued; when the queue is not
re
adable the report says `retractUnavailable` instead of claiming a clean queue.

A plan nobody will press again closes itself. After a restart by hand, finishing those sessions
your

self is enough: each stopped turn is seen living on, moved forward and no longer running, so the
pla

n settles the way a completed restore does and the button returns to pause, with no press. Only
turn

s the pause itself stopped are considered, and only on positive evidence: a session still working,
a
session list that cannot be read, or an error keeps the plan exactly as it was.
## How resume works
A restore is not a claim that work continued. It is three honest steps per item:
1. **Mount.** A stopped session is mounted through the Harness resume path, which preserves its agen

t
preset. If it is already mounted, that step is skipped.
2. **Continue, only where the press actual

ly cancelled a turn.** The continuation is one ordinary
user message sent through `sessionController

.prompt`, with a request id derived from the plan and
the session. The id makes a repeated restore i

dempotent, and the message is visible in the
transcript, so the person can see exactly what was resu

med.
3. **Re-arm a goal** with the revision it had when paused. The revision is the person's veto: i

f the
goal changed while paused, it is not ours to resume and the item is `skipped`.
Every attempt is journaled with the id of the process that made it, but a journal is reporting, not

a
promise: the next boot asks the live Harness again instead of trusting an old row. The continuatio

n
request id is derived from the plan and the session, so a retry before a turn starts is deduplicat

ed
by the Host. A failure leaves the plan on disk and the next press retries every item that still n

Host. A failure leaves the plan on disk and the next press retries every item that still needs
work.
A subagent session cannot be mounted by this process: its parent chat owns the routing. That row is
reported once as attention for the parent, not retried as a failure, so it never keeps the plan open
eported once as attention for the parent, not retried as a failure, so it never keeps the plan open.
## Crash, not just a press

A press writes a snapshot. A crash writes nothing, so the plugin keeps a heartbeat instead:
`running

.json` holds the sessions whose turn is open right now and the id of the process that wrote
it. The

previous process's record is turned into a crash plan in `pending.json` before the heartbeat
file is

replaced, so a second or third restart still sees the same work and offers ▶ with no press
needed.
A crash record is weaker than a press: it proves a session existed, not that a turn was open after t

he
restart. Restore attaches every recorded session and reads the live turn. A row whose turn is sti

ll
running is continued; a row that is idle is left idle by the probe, which mounts it to read it an

d does
not prompt it. A row whose state cannot be read or proven is reported as unknown, and unknown

is not
finished: the plan stays on disk, the button keeps offering ▶, and the next press tries agai

n. A
